title: Protection Fee Charging Rules of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
The protection fee under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan is arrived at on the level's own charging basis,
and the three bases are not interchangeable. On a daily flat basis the fee is the level's daily amount multiplied
by the charged days. On a percentage basis it is the level's percentage of the trip price. On a greater-of basis
both are worked out and the larger of the two is taken, so that neither a cheap long trip nor an expensive short
one escapes the fee.

A fee line is posted only while the election is in the elected or active state, since a quote that was never
chosen is never charged.

## The three bases side by side

| The level's basis | What the fee comes to |
|---|---|
| A daily flat amount | The level's daily amount multiplied by the charged days |
| A share of the trip price | The level's percentage of the trip price |
| The greater of the two | Both are worked out and the larger of the two is taken |

## The state the election must stand in

The election reference correlates the fee line to the election, and the state standing on that election record
is read before the line is posted. The elected state and the active state both admit a fee line; a quote that
was never chosen does not, since it was never chosen.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this policy are no longer in force, having been superseded on the current basis of the
Keyturn Guest Protection Plan. They are recorded here so that the wording is not applied:

1. "Additional drivers are charged the level's additional driver fee once each for the whole trip, not once for each day, and a level that carries no additional driver fee charges nothing however many drivers are approved." — no longer in force.
2. "A driver under the young-driver threshold pays the level's protection surcharge on the fee, and the surcharge is posted as its own line so that it can be reversed on its own." — no longer in force.
3. "Charged days are the whole days of the trip as reserved, with any part day counted as a whole day, and never fewer than the level's minimum charge days." — no longer in force.
4. "The fee falls due at the level's billing point, whether at booking, at the start of the trip or daily in arrears, and a level billed daily in arrears posts one line for each completed day rather than one line for the trip." — no longer in force.
5. "The fee arrived at is then held between the level's floor and its ceiling, the floor applied first and the ceiling last, so a trip long enough to pass the ceiling pays the ceiling and no more." — no longer in force.

The per-level figures those clauses referred to remain recorded against the levels of the Keyturn Guest
Protection Plan; the clauses above are not applied to a charge.

## A worked reading of the bases on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical trip of 4 charged days priced at 120.00 USD a day, so that the trip price is 480.00 USD.
On a level written on a daily flat amount of 30.00 USD the fee comes to 120.00 USD. On a level written as 20
percent of the trip price the fee comes to 96.00 USD. On a level written on the greater of the two, both
figures are worked out and the larger, 120.00 USD, is taken. Lengthen the same hypothetical trip to 20 charged
days and the trip price becomes 2400.00 USD: the daily basis gives 600.00 USD, the percentage basis 480.00 USD,
and the greater-of basis again takes the larger of the two.
